notes:
ATTEMPT 3. Still FAIL, and the reason is a measurement error of mine that ran through all three attempts.

No attempt so far was ever aimed at the correct geometry. Attempts 1 and 2 were generated from a prompt whose GEOMETRY LOCK read 'the notch between the lapel and the collar opens at 68 degrees' - it took the 68 in the option's NAME to be the notch angle. The model obeyed, and QC correctly measured 'close to a right angle'. For attempt 3 I corrected that to 'a NARROW HORIZONTAL SLIT, its two edges nearly parallel', which I had read off the drawing at thumbnail size. The model obeyed that too, and produced 10.3 degrees.

Only now has the drawing actually been MEASURED. Rendering it at 1000px, zooming the frame-left notch 4x and overlaying a percent grid resolves three strokes meeting at a node - the collar's lower edge, the lapel's upper edge, and the gorge seam. Law of cosines on the node and the two tips gives 39.8 degrees, confirmed independently by the direction angles of the two edges (156.6 and 166.9 measured from the node). The drawn notch is a TIGHT BUT GENUINELY OPEN wedge of about 40 degrees.

So the sequence is: 68 specified -> 90 rendered; 'nearly parallel' specified -> 10 rendered; against a true 40. The option has never once been asked for the right shape.

This is the cb-5 lesson a second time: AN INHERITED OR EYEBALLED MEASUREMENT IS NOT EVIDENCE. A number in a label is not a measurement of the drawing, and a shape read off a thumbnail is not a measurement either. Both times the model faithfully rendered what it was told, and both times what it was told was wrong.

What did land: the gorge is now correctly arced and correctly high, the lapel edge pitch measures ~70 against 62-68 drawn, and composition and construction are clean. The failure is isolated to the notch opening.

Recorded as attempt 3 of 3, which closes this run.
